reviewScope: Both related articles rewritten after parent expanded the assignment.
Existing URLs and all previous article heading anchors retained.
keyCorrections: Winter protection distinguished by cultivar, root/graft status, climbing framework, high graft and container root exposure.
First light frost and fixed November/April dates replaced with acclimation, soil state, forecast, ventilation and spring growth conditions.
Universal 5–10 cm graft burial replaced with an attributed local approximate 5 cm instruction for ordinary bed roses, grower-specific follow-up, and explicit standard/own-root exceptions.
No promise that all park roses or all Canadian cultivars overwinter without protection.
No universal short autumn pruning. Once-flowering shrub and rambler wood retained; repeat-flowering groups treated separately.
Corrected the former reversed recommendation to prune floribundas harder than hybrid teas.
Removed unsupported folklore, horsetail cure, household soap treatment, obligatory compost tea and wound sealant advice.
Black spot management no longer prescribes automatic fungicide applications every 7–14 days. Current VAAD permitted use and product-specific label control the decision.
Removed absolute wet-leaf-equals-disease statement; distinguished black spot from mildew and non-specific yellowing.

sourceInterpretation.localPlantingDepth: 7rozes gives 5 cm below soil for ordinary grafted roses. RHS UK planting page instead gives soil level. The guide attributes the local recommendation and does not present one depth as valid for all stock, forms or climates.
sourceInterpretation.foreignClimate: UK and US calendar dates, USDA zone examples and cultivar hardiness guarantees were not transferred to Latvia.
sourceInterpretation.containerTemperature: Iowa State 30–45 F translated approximately to −1 to +7 C; used as a monitored dormant-storage reference, not an outdoor hardiness threshold.
sourceInterpretation.standardRoses: Soil hilling at ground level does not protect a high graft. Tipping is described as a separate root-ball-aware method, not instructions to force a rigid trunk.
sourceInterpretation.diseaseRecipes: Primary sources used for identification, sanitation and care. Foreign pesticide names and timing excluded; no product availability claims made.
sourceInterpretation.compost: Diseased leaf handling avoids a blanket prohibition on all composting; uncontrolled cold home compost is distinguished from reliable pathogen treatment.
